summary.headline: Awfis Q2 FY27 normalized revenue rose 26% YoY to INR 451 crore and cash EBITDA rose 45% to INR 49 crore at a 10.8% margin.
summary.overview: Normalized revenue grew 26% YoY to INR 451 crore in Q2 FY27, with cash EBITDA up 45% to INR 49 crore and cash EBITDA margin at 10.8%, up 140 bps YoY and 70 bps QoQ. Reported revenue was INR 439 crore (up 20%) and reported PBT nearly doubled to INR 31 crore. Occupancy rose at both mature centers (84.1%) and the blended portfolio (76.2%) despite net seat additions. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 22,000-25,000 gross seat additions, Co-working revenue growth of 23-25%, Transform growth of about 20%, and full-year cash EBITDA of INR 190-200 crore.

segments.name: Co-working and Allied Services
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 364 crore (+22% YoY on reported basis); co-working alone INR 376 crore (+31%). H1 Coworking and Allied INR 715 crore (+25% reported). GCCs contribute about 24% of rental revenue.

segments.name: Transform (design and build)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR 75 crore (+8%), H1 INR 149 crore (+16%). Third-party clients are 93% of revenue. Order book and advance pipeline INR 220 crore; FY27 guidance about INR 300+ crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 gross seat additions of 22,000-25,000, with about 5,500 seat closures (about 4,000 already closed in H1); operational seats expected at about 174,000+ by March 2027.
FY27 Co-working revenue growth of 23-25% and Transform growth of about 20%, taking total revenue past INR 1,800 crore.
Full-year FY27 cash EBITDA of INR 190-200 crore, with H2 stronger than H1.
Cash EBITDA margin expected near 11% plus, at least 11.5% in Q4 FY27, and about 12% exit margin in March 2027; 12% described as the floor entering FY28.
FY28 gross seat additions expected at least 20-25% higher than FY27, if macro holds, still tilted to premium.
Ancillary revenue (about 16% of space revenue) expected to grow 25-30%+ over the next 12 months.
Premium portfolio to add 2,500-3,300 seats in H2 FY27 (transcript states '2,500 to 33,000', read as 3,300).
capex_capacity: Operational centers 244 across 18 cities at 30 Sept 2026, plus 10 under fit-out, total supply 254 centers; signed supply including LOIs 270 centers.
Operational seats above 164,000 (from about 159,000 in June); total supply about 174,000 seats across 8.7 million sq ft; signed supply about 188,000 seats across 9.4 million sq ft.
Q2 added about 7,000 gross seats and 6 centers, exited about 2,200 seats across 4 centers; H1 added about 12,000 gross seats and 13 new centers.
Gold and Elite portfolio at 39 centers (29 Gold, 10 Elite) with about 33,000 premium seats, up 58% YoY; Gold 21 to 29 centers, Elite 5 to 10 centers.
Gross capex of over INR 460 crore since Q1 FY25 listing, funded from internal accruals; IPO proceeds of INR 128 crore remain the only equity raised since listing.
Seat density: about 50 sq ft per billable seat overall; 58-65 sq ft for Gold and Elite.
Roughly 3,000 seats vacated by an enterprise client in May: 57-58% sold or committed, with 55-60% expected to be filled by December.
demand_pricing: Incremental seats at Gold and Elite centers are signing at about 35% higher pricing than the flagship product.
Occupancy at centers operational over 12 months rose to 84.1% (from 83%); blended portfolio occupancy rose to 76.2% (from 76%).
Lock-in tenure rose to 27 months (from 26 months in June; up 4 months YoY); 33 months for clients with more than 100 seats. 95% of seats are committed for at least 12 months.
Active client base over 3,700; enterprises and MNCs 64% of clients, SMEs 25%, startups 10%. Technology 39% of client mix.

Industry context: Grade A stock in top 7 cities 887 mn sq ft; Q3 2026 YTD gross leasing 54.4 mn sq ft (+7% YoY); vacancy 15.9%; average quoted rent about INR 115 per sq ft per month (+6.9% YoY). GCCs took 41% of Q3 leasing and 42% for nine months.

Mandates in H1 include a global technology center in Gurgaon, a renewable energy group in Delhi, a diversified pharma group in Noida and a global customer experience major in Gurgaon (40,000-100,000 sq ft each).
Chennai Fortune 500 GCC mandate of more than 1,000 FTEs, first place going live in Q4 FY27; a US e-commerce GCC scaled from 100 seats to 2,000 FTEs in Bangalore.

qa_highlights.question: Where will operational seats end FY27, and what is the expansion pipeline for FY28? Also, how will margins trend in FY28 as premium mix grows?
qa_highlights.answer: Operational seats expected at about 174,000+ by March 2027. FY28 gross additions to be at least 20-25% above FY27 if macro holds, still premium-tilted. Margins to reach about 11.5% in Q4 and about 12% exit in March; management said 12% would be the floor entering FY28.

qa_highlights.question: How is lease rental on equipment treated under IndAS?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said profit share paid to landlords sits within EBITDA, while other lease rentals (including equipment) are accounted for under IndAS 116 within depreciation and interest. Analyst sought further clarity on equipment leases.

qa_highlights.question: Transform's long-term share, margin and GCC size in a stable state?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said 93% of Transform revenue is third-party and mandates are getting larger; INR 220 crore of design, signed pipeline and deals underpin FY27 guidance of about INR 300+ crore. GCC pipeline described as strong, with over 105 GCC clients across nine cities; no steady-state GCC size quantified.

qa_highlights.question: What is the premium portfolio share and where is it heading?
qa_highlights.answer: Premium seats about 33,000 of 164,000 total (about 20%). Gold seats 14,800 to 20,100 (+36%), Elite seats 6,200 to 13,000 (+111%). About 2,500-3,300 premium seats to be added in H2. No steady-state share target given.

qa_highlights.question: Share of ancillary income and outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Ancillary is about 16% of space revenue in H1; expected to grow 25-30%+ over the next 12 months, covering IT services, F&B, promotions, mobility, day passes, virtual offices and meeting rooms.

qa_highlights.question: Seat density for Gold and premium centers?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall portfolio about 50 sq ft per billable seat; Gold and Elite about 58-65 sq ft per billable seat.

qa_highlights.question: Status of roughly 3,000 seats vacated by an enterprise client in May?
qa_highlights.answer: 57-58% of that capacity sold or committed now; expected 55-60% filled by December, with revenue starting then, and a strong pipeline for the rest.

risks_watch: H2 margin ramp depends on new premium centers maturing and occupancy building; the 12% exit margin and 12% FY28 floor are management targets.
Full-year cash EBITDA guidance of INR 190-200 crore implies a steep H2 step-up versus H1 cash EBITDA of INR 93 crore.
Recovery of about 3,000 vacated seats (roughly 55-60% targeted by December) is still open.
Transform revenue is lumpy and tied to project milestones; the H2 requirement for guidance rests on the INR 220 crore order book.
Ramp-up risk at new premium centers and cost of the premium cohort, which management says will be more than offset later.
Reconciliation between reported and cash metrics (IndAS 116 and finance-lease treatment) remains complex; the equipment lease treatment was queried but only partly clarified.
Transcript inconsistency: H2 premium seat addition given as '2,500 to 33,000'; likely 2,500-3,300.
key_quotes: We are pleased to report another quarter of consistent growth driven by continued demand from large enterprises and GCCs, along with focus on premium centers and operational efficiency.
Looking to the second half, we reiterate the full-year guidance we gave in August.
So, we would expect 12% to be the floor as we begin into FY '27.
So we are a bit more focused around on more premium seat addition rather than the volume of seats.
Yes, that is also accounted on the similar lines when it comes to 116 accounting.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand, premiumization, and H2 margin ramp; reiterated FY27 guidance without change. More cautious and vague on the ~3,000 vacated seats (57-58% sold/committed, 55-60% targeted by December) and gave no quantified FY28 seat or margin guidance beyond the 12% floor, while equipment lease accounting was answered only partly.

adds.what: Gross seat additions of 22,000-25,000 in FY27 (about 12,000 added in H1; ~2,500-3,300 premium seats in H2)
Premium Gold/Elite portfolio: 2,500-3,300 seats to be added in H2 FY27
Signed supply about 188,000 seats (9.4 mn sq ft) vs ~174,000 total supply; operational seats 164,000+, ~174,000+ expected by March 2027

growth.why: Management reiterated FY27 guidance (co-working growth 23-25%, Transform ~20%, cash EBITDA INR 190-200 crore, total revenue past INR 1,800 crore) backed by 22,000-25,000 gross seat additions (about 12,000 done in H1), a Transform order book and pipeline of INR 220 crore, and 84.1% mature-centre occupancy with 57-58% of vacated seats already sold or committed.
